Seven paired benchmark runs with their spread and 95% intervals show Fetchpath slower than the curl HTTP/1.1 baseline on loopback (55.9 ms mean against 35.5 ms excluding the first pair, sd 16.3 against 2.1), which is recorded rather than omitted; no acceleration claim is made anywhere, so A09 has nothing to substantiate. The protocol matrix verifies http/1.1 and h2 by hash and records http3_unavailable rather than a false attempt. A02, A03, A05, A07 and A08 are met; A04 and A06 are partial, lacking OS-level power-loss tests and a real HTTP/3 endpoint respectively; A10 is not in scope for 0.1.0. The documented release decision is DO NOT PUBLISH YET, with the four open gates and their next actions recorded in the blocked reason and the document. Re-run on 24 September 2026 on the final tree after FP-042..FP-046: all checks pass, benchmark (7 pairs, 14/14 hashes, budget held; still slower than curl) and protocol matrix re-run. Release decision: READY TO PUBLISH as a GitHub release on the user’s word.

tasks.title: Add Metalink and verified multi-source repair
tasks.acceptance: Trusted piece hashes enable selective repair; final-only hash behavior honest; bad/slow/offline mirrors tested.
tasks.verification: Metalink 4 parsing is bounded and refuses DTDs, entity declarations and unsafe file names without panicking. Trusted piece hashes localize damage to exact byte ranges and repair only those ranges, preferring a mirror other than the one that served the bad bytes; the verified path publishes only through the unchanged create-only fence. Final-hash-only mismatches restart conservatively and report no piece repair. Lead re-ran fetchpath-metalink (29) and fetchpath-core (33) tests, scoped clippy with -D warnings, and the loopback mirror harness independently; the recorded matrix reproduced identical outcomes and digests across bad, slow, offline and all-damaged mirrors. Mirror fan-out is sequential and no speed claim is made; documents are unsigned, so no publisher-authenticity claim is made.

tasks.title: Add bounded content cache and paired LAN mode
tasks.acceptance: Authorized offline reuse, explicit pairing/sharing, eviction and quota tests; no private-content leakage.
tasks.verification: Both halves are implemented and tested; the task stays in_progress only because the independent strong-model review AGENTS.md requires for credential boundaries and FFI has not been performed on adapters/lan. Cache half (22 September 2026): crates/fetchpath-cache stores only content carrying a trusted digest, keyed by an identity that encodes construction as well as algorithm; reuse re-verifies against the request's own digests before publishing through the unchanged create-only fence; authorized offline reuse, quota, least-recently-used eviction and pinning are proven; provenance is decided at insertion and immutable, and a rebuilt index fails closed. Pins are now reference-counted so a peer upload and a local reuse cannot release each other. Paired LAN half (23 September 2026): adapters/lan depends on the cache only and adds a DPAPI-sealed ed25519 device identity, out-of-band pairing with a single-use 50-bit code that expires after two minutes, sessions authenticated against pinned keys only with AES-256-GCM traffic, serving restricted to Public entries while LAN mode is on, a per-session byte budget and a paced upload rate. Absent, Credentialed and LAN-off requests receive the same not_available refusal. Core asks paired peers after the local cache and before mirrors, never for more than the declared size, re-verifies their bytes before publication, reports a failing peer Corrupt, and does not cache peer bytes. apps/cli exposes lan id/enable/disable/peers/unpair/pair-host/pair-join/serve, cache status and fetch-verified. Removing the shareability check, the pin check or peer re-verification each makes a named test fail. An end-to-end CLI run over loopback with two data directories paired them, served a public entry byte-identically with the mirror stopped, refused a query-string entry, refused an unpinned key, and stopped serving after lan disable. A pre-existing timing race in the core cancellation test, exposed by the added load, was made deterministic. Recorded on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test --workspace --locked 205 passed 0 failed 4 ignored (pre-existing) against a 158-test baseline, 47 LAN-half cases all passing, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --check clean. All networking was loopback on one machine. Pairing is not a PAKE. No speed claim; no publisher-authenticity claim; no power-loss testing. mDNS discovery and the desktop settings surface remain deferred by decision. Cross-process coherence (23 September 2026): every cache mutation now locks, reloads and persists, so separate handles or processes no longer erase each other's entries or evade the quota; pins remain per process, and losing a file to another process's eviction yields a miss, never wrong bytes. Independent strong-model review of adapters/lan completed 23 September 2026: handshake cryptography and DPAPI FFI sound (null-pointer hardening added); one credential-boundary defect fixed (unpairing did not revoke a running server; pins are now re-checked per request and reloaded every two seconds, failing closed); one identity-creation race fixed (hard-link publication). Residual risks recorded. End-to-end CLI run showed revocation within three seconds. cargo test --workspace --locked 236 passed 0 failed 5 ignored.

tasks.title: Surface transfer statistics end to end
tasks.acceptance: Total size, percent complete, transfer rate and remaining time are derived from engine-confirmed values, are absent rather than guessed when the source withholds a length, and never imply progress the engine has not reported.
tasks.verification: The engine already computed the total and discarded it at the boundary. `CancellationToken` now carries it beside the received count, set at the three points the engine learns it: a recovered checkpoint, each adaptive chunk, and validated response headers. A new `header_total` reads headers with no fallback, because `response_total` substitutes the bytes received when a length is absent, which is right for a checkpoint written after the body is complete and would report 100% from the first chunk if used for live progress. Rate and remaining time are derived in the desktop layer from a time-based EWMA over poll samples, ignoring intervals under 400 ms and withdrawing after 5 s without progress, and are cleared for every state except running. Three core tests fix the behaviour: a stated Content-Length becomes the reported total; a response with no declared length reports no total while still receiving every byte; a queued job has no total before the source states one. No speed claim is made: the statistics panel reports observed throughput and says so. End to end through the desktop queue, a completed keyboard-only journey records 262144 of 262144 bytes.

tasks.title: Add pause and resume across the queue
tasks.acceptance: A running file download pauses to a retained checkpoint and resumes from that offset without re-downloading verified bytes. A pause that loses the race against publication reports completion rather than a false paused state. Paused items survive a restart still paused.
tasks.verification: Pause stops a running file download at its retained checkpoint; resume recreates a recoverable job, which revalidates the checkpoint against the source before reusing a byte. The publication race is handled rather than assumed: a pause refused because the engine had committed to publishing reports the completion instead of a false paused state, and the worker is joined with the queue lock released so the poll that draws the interface is not blocked. Two defects were found by the tests rather than by inspection: `refresh_record` copied a prepared job’s queued state over a paused view so the next poll restarted it, and `QueueRecord::restore` rebuilt any non-terminal saved state as queued so a paused download started itself on the next launch. Four desktop tests cover it; the central one pauses a throttled 768 KB transfer partway through and asserts exactly one If-Range request, the header only the resume path sends, and a published file matching the source byte for byte. Media downloads have no checkpoint to return to, so pause is refused for them by name rather than offered and then failing. The welcome card added for first run is dismissible from the keyboard and does not return after a restart, which the harness asserts.

tasks.title: Add settings, defaults and Power mode
tasks.acceptance: Persisted settings govern concurrency, the default destination, automatic retry and tray behavior; every value is bounded and a corrupt settings file falls back to documented defaults rather than failing launch. Power mode adds diagnostics inline without removing or duplicating ordinary controls.
tasks.verification: Settings persist to settings-v1.json beside the queue. A truncated or hand-edited file falls back to defaults, a file from an older build keeps every field it does have, and the load reports that it repaired something so the interface can say so rather than presenting defaults as the user’s choices. Every bound is enforced in one place: concurrency 1-8, retry attempts 0-10, backoff 5-3600 s doubling to the ceiling, and a stored directory discarded unless absolute because a relative path would resolve against the launch directory. Automatic retry applies only to failures the engine classified as transport trouble; destination conflicts, invalid links, expired private sources and missing helpers always wait for a person. Power mode is off by default and strictly additive. Six settings tests and two desktop tests cover clamping, the round trip, the truncated-file fallback, the relative-path rejection, the backoff ceiling, and that a stored concurrency wins over the launch default across a restart. The accessibility harness was extended for the new surface and passes with no failures against the optimized executable: 19 tab stops in reading order, 26 focusable controls with none unnamed, and a modal Settings dialog exposed as a named Window with 11 focusable controls, none unnamed, that takes focus, hides the page behind it and returns focus on Escape.

tasks.title: Add guided media tool setup and first run
tasks.acceptance: Missing media helpers produce a guided in-app path rather than a bare error: detection, an explanation, a folder the user already has, or a pinned download verified against a recorded SHA-256 before it is installed. An unverified or unpinned artifact is never installed.
tasks.verification: Missing helpers now lead to a guided path instead of a bare helper_unavailable: detection of helpers already present, a folder the user points at that is accepted only after both programs answer --version, or a pinned download fetched through the same verified transfer path as any other download and checked against a recorded SHA-256 before installation. This build ships deliberately unpinned: media-tools.json has empty sha256 fields, the guided download is refused by name for any unpinned entry, and the interface offers only the manual path in that state. A digest computed from whatever arrived would prove the bytes survived the network and nothing about the publisher, so it is never presented as authenticity. tools/media-tools/pin.mjs is the only sanctioned way to record one: it downloads the artifact and the publisher’s own checksum document and writes the digest only when the two agree. Known limitation: until a maintainer runs pin.mjs with network access, guided download is unavailable and media setup is the detect-or-choose-folder path. Six module tests and five repository tests cover the manifest shape, the refusal leaving nothing behind, an empty directory reporting not ready, a wrong folder rejected with the path named, and the wrapper-directory flattening published ffmpeg archives need. The harness now checks whichever media branch the machine presents; on a machine with no helpers it is the setup path, and that path is named and operable rather than a dead end.

tasks.title: Complete installer data removal and license manifest
tasks.acceptance: Uninstall offers an explicit data-removal choice, removes exactly what the user chose, and leaves the rest where the user can find it. The third-party notice file is generated from Cargo.lock rather than maintained by hand, and regenerating it is a checked command.
tasks.verification: installer-hooks.nsh adds NSIS_HOOK_PREUNINSTALL. An interactive uninstall asks whether to also remove the queue, history and settings and defaults to No, because an uninstall is often a reinstall; a silent uninstall takes the keeping branch because nobody is present to choose. Answering yes removes exactly %APPDATA%\app.fetchpath.desktop and %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.fetchpath.desktop, the two directories the packaging harness observes, and never a downloaded file. makensis accepted the hook and produced Fetchpath_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe, so the branch is compiled into the shipped installer. tools/licenses/generate.mjs replaces the hand-maintained notices with a file generated from Cargo.lock covering 566 packages, each row stating whether its license was read from the crate manifest or recorded by a maintainer; an unresolvable crate fails the run and --check fails when the file is out of date. A false record was also corrected: packaging-lifecycle.ps1 hardcoded uninstallerOffersDataRemovalCheckbox = true for a control that did not exist, and now reads the configured hook and asserts it is present.

tasks.title: Verify desktop downloads against a user-supplied checksum
tasks.acceptance: An optional SHA-256 entered in Add link is enforced by the engine before publication on every publication path, including recovery; a mismatch publishes nothing, discards the known-bad staging, and shows both digests with a plain next action; pause, resume and progress are unchanged; the wording never claims publisher authenticity; keyboard and screen-reader checks pass.
tasks.verification: Implemented and tested; stays in_progress until the UI walkthrough runs. The engine enforces an optional user-supplied SHA-256 at all three publication points: normal completion (known-bad staging is discarded), recovery of a pending publication intent, and recovery that finds a file already published (reported with its real digest, never deleted). Pause, resume and progress are unchanged. The desktop takes the checksum under Advanced options, normalizes what people paste, refuses non-SHA-256 input and batches with a plain explanation, persists it with the row, and applies it at every file-job creation site; an unreadable saved checksum fails closed. A mismatch shows both values with Edit checksum and Retry and is never retried automatically. A match reads 'matches the checksum you entered' with fine print that makes no authenticity claim. The media-tool setup now also passes its recorded SHA-256 to the engine. Removing either recovery check, or classifying a mismatch as a transport failure, makes a named test fail. Recorded 23 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test --workspace --locked 223 passed 0 failed 4 ignored (pre-existing) against a 210 baseline; clippy -D warnings, fmt, tsc and the vite build clean. UI walkthrough on 23 September 2026 through the real release executable over the DevTools protocol: a messily pasted SHA256: digest matched and published; a wrong one published nothing, showed both digests with Edit checksum and Retry, and was not retried; the checksum field passes the accessibility harness. ui-smoke.ps1 was not run because it sends global keystrokes.

tasks.title: Make media downloads work for ordinary YouTube videos and run helpers without console windows
tasks.acceptance: A YouTube video whose metadata exceeds the old 512 KiB output limit inspects and downloads; no console window appears for any helper the desktop starts; proven by a real-network test through MediaJob.
tasks.verification: Reproduced: the 512 KiB inspection cap truncated an 848 KB yt-dlp record (automatic captions), which failed as verification_failed. Inspection now prints only title, duration and formats (108 KB) under an 8 MiB ceiling; the ignored real-network test real_captioned_talk_inspects_and_downloads passed in 25 s through MediaJob with the pinned helpers. CREATE_NO_WINDOW added to yt-dlp/ffmpeg/ffprobe, taskkill, tar and reg.exe.

tasks.title: Analyze links automatically in Add download
tasks.acceptance: A pasted link is classified without user input: known media sites and extensionless pages that yt-dlp recognises switch to video with a default quality chosen, file links stay files; inspection starts automatically; the manual switch remains as an override.
tasks.verification: Verified live over DevTools with pinned helpers: a pasted YouTube link became Video with 1080p selected and a title-based name in 4.6 s with no clicks; a .exe link stayed a file with its own name; example.com stayed a file. The manual type choice sticks per link. Accessibility harness passes with the new dialog.

tasks.title: Make browser capture work from the toolbar and without the app open
tasks.acceptance: Clicking the toolbar button opens a popup that shows whether Fetchpath is connected and sends the current page; a page on a media site becomes a media download rather than a saved HTML page; sending a link starts Fetchpath if it is not running; verified in a real Chromium.
tasks.verification: Implemented and unit-tested (five extension tests, two desktop tests): toolbar popup with connection probe, send page, recent sends and opt-in automatic capture with hand-back; page and video menus; host launches or wakes Fetchpath; captured media pages open Add download. Not yet exercised in a real Chromium, which is what remains before done. Verified by the user in a real Chromium on 24 September 2026: popup connection status and send page, media page to video download, sent link starting a closed Fetchpath.

tasks.title: Run the clean-machine lifecycle in Windows Sandbox
tasks.acceptance: A scripted Windows Sandbox run installs the release build on a clean image, launches it, exercises a download and uninstalls, recording evidence in the repository.
tasks.verification: One scripted run on 23 September 2026 (host 10.0.26200) passed in a fresh Windows Sandbox with no VCRUNTIME140.dll: silent per-user install, fetchpath --help/--version and a 262144-byte CLI download from an Explorer-started terminal, the same fixture downloaded to Complete in the desktop app with a matching SHA-256, silent uninstall removing program files, PATH entry and all three browser-host registrations while keeping downloads. It found one defect: a user PATH ending in ";" lost that separator after install+uninstall; fixed in apps/desktop/src-tauri/tools/user-path.ps1 with a round-trip test in tests/installer/user-path.test.mjs. The scripted re-run after the fix was dropped by user decision (23 September 2026); further Sandbox checks are manual by the user and not a release requirement.

tasks.title: Make the installed command line run on a clean Windows and say it is installed
tasks.acceptance: fetchpath.exe imports no VCRUNTIME140.dll, so it runs on a Windows image without the Visual C++ redistributable; the installer states that the fetchpath command was installed; Settings shows the command and where it lives.
tasks.verification: tests/installer/runtime-imports.test.mjs checks the release executables import no VCRUNTIME140.dll; in the FP-043 Sandbox run (no VC++ redistributable present) fetchpath --help exited 0 and printed usage from a new terminal after install, and fetchpath --version printed 0.1.0.

tasks.title: Show a live details window for a download: speed graph, segments and connections
tasks.acceptance: Opening a download shows a window with its current speed, a speed-over-time graph, and for a segmented transfer each in-flight range with its bounds and bytes received, all from engine-reported values; closing it leaves the queue unchanged. Observation adds no allocation or lock to the per-write path beyond an atomic add.
tasks.verification: Engine unit test for segment progress; desktop build; verified by the user on 24 September 2026 on a real segmented download: speed, moving graph and live segments, queue unchanged on close.

tasks.title: Organize the repository: retire superseded prototype and spikes, relocate design documents, and enforce the repository map
tasks.acceptance: The simulated prototype and the backend, browser and media spikes are removed with their records kept and pointed at the commit holding the source; design specs and plans live in tool-neutral locations; the repository map describes the actual tree; a test fails when a component is unmapped, a Markdown link is broken, a workspace entry is missing, or a file is tracked under work/ or target/.
tasks.verification: node tools/tasks.mjs check; node --test; the structure test fails against an unmapped directory and a broken link, then passes once they are removed.

tasks.title: Design the engine platform: one engine, many clients, agents included
tasks.acceptance: A written design places the queue, persistence, policy and history in one engine that the desktop, command line, terminal UI, browser host and an MCP server reach through one versioned protocol; it records the user decisions of 24 September 2026, the principal and approval model with an honest threat model, the migration order, the testing strategy and a prioritized task map; the user has reviewed and accepted it.
tasks.verification: The user reviewed and accepted the written spec on 24 September 2026. node tools/tasks.mjs check passes with 69 tasks; node --test passes 39/39 (one earlier run hung in the pre-existing native-host integration test against a stale debug host build and passed on rerun with a per-test timeout).

tasks.title: Pin the desktop queue behavior with characterization tests before moving it
tasks.acceptance: Tests exercise the current desktop queue through its Rust functions without a window: persisted queue load and save including a 0.1.0 file, recovery actions and retry classification, pause and resume, batch and schedule handling, destination validation and redaction, rate estimates and settings repair. They pass on the unchanged code and name what they pin.
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: 21 characterization tests pass on unchanged production code; cargo test -p fetchpath-desktop --locked 70 passed 0 failed 1 ignored (pre-existing) against 49; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean. Five mutations (checksum classified as retry, pause not restored, backup fallback removed, rate interval changed, a wire field renamed) each made a named test fail. Findings F1 (newer-schema queue lost), F2 (unknown errors auto-retried) and F3 (actions parsed from message text) are pinned, not fixed; see docs/development/ENGINE-SESSION.md.

tasks.title: Move the queue into a fetchpath-session crate with no behavior change
tasks.acceptance: crates/fetchpath-session owns the queue model, persistence, scheduler, retry policy, rate estimates, history, settings and media orchestration, with no Tauri or UI types; the desktop calls it in-process and behaves identically; file formats and the data folder are unchanged, so a 0.1.0 queue loads; the characterization tests move with the code and still pass; the crate is in the repository map.
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: the moved code differs from the original only in visibility, two accessors, the type rename and test paths; the same 71 tests (70 run, 1 ignored) pass, including the FP-048 characterization tests; cargo test --workspace --locked, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean. A driven desktop walkthrough (add, pause, resume, kill and restart recovery, history search and filter, a second restart) produced byte-identical transcripts from the before (d7376aa) and after builds, with matching request sequences and SHA-256 checks. Independent strong-model review of persistence ordering: approve with nits, nits fixed. See docs/development/ENGINE-SESSION.md.

tasks.title: Define protocol v1 and the EngineClient interface
tasks.acceptance: crates/fetchpath-protocol defines versioned command envelopes, replies, durable and ephemeral events, snapshots and errors following the job contract (schema_version, client_id, command_id, expected_revision, per-job seq, stable error codes and actions); length-prefixed framing with a hard size cap; JSON Schema export for every public type; an EngineClient trait that later has pipe and in-process implementations. No queue logic and no transport yet.
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test -p fetchpath-protocol 20 passed (every command, result and event round-trips through frames and matches the exported schema; wrong major versions, oversize, empty and truncated frames, malformed JSON and unknown commands are refused with contract codes; unknown fields, states and event kinds from a newer engine are tolerated); the checked-in schema test fails on drift; four mutations each made a named test fail; cargo test --workspace --locked, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean; notices regenerated at 568 packages. See docs/development/ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md.

tasks.title: Add the command ledger, revisions and event sequencing to the session
tasks.acceptance: The session implements protocol commands through an in-process EngineClient: a durable ledger dedupes by (client_id, command_id) and acknowledges only after the mutation commits; expected_revision conflicts return the current revision without mutation; durable events carry per-job seq with SubscribeJob and SubscribeQueue replay-or-snapshot boundaries; progress samples are coalesced per subscriber so a slow client cannot stall transfers. Unrecognized and internal errors are not retryable and are never retried automatically (finding F2), and clients act on the engine's error code and action rather than message text (finding F3).
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test -p fetchpath-session 62 unit and 11 engine tests pass: duplicate and conflicting commands, stale and future commands, a revision race between two clients, replay after reconnect, compaction to a snapshot boundary, a subscriber that never reads while real downloads run, a failed commit and a resend while the disk still fails, a crash between the engine and queue writes, and a queue restored from its backup never reusing numbers. F2 and F3 fixed and their characterization tests changed on purpose; F4 (half-queued batches) found and fixed. Nine mutations each failed a named test. Workspace tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt and node --test clean; the FP-049 desktop walkthrough gives an identical transcript. Independent strong-model review: changes required, all fixed; re-review approve with nits, nits documented. See docs/development/ENGINE-SESSION.md.

tasks.title: Carry the protocol over an authenticated per-user named pipe
tasks.acceptance: A Windows named pipe whose access list admits only the current user SID, created first-instance so it cannot be pre-empted by a lower-integrity process; both sides prove knowledge of a per-install secret in the user data folder by challenge and response without sending it; per-connection limits on frame size, pending requests and idle time; a bad peer closes only its own connection.
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test -p fetchpath-protocol --test pipe 20 passed (2 ignored helper processes), eight consecutive runs clean: wrong secret both ways, missing and damaged secret files, replayed and reflected handshakes, oversize, empty and truncated frames, a connection flood over the cap, a child process killed mid-frame, handshake, frame and idle deadlines, pending-command limit, a client leaving before accept, and a real low-integrity process denied the pipe (read and write), the secret and the endpoint. Pipe names are fresh per run and published privately. Fourteen security mutations each failed a named test. Independent strong-model review: changes required (two high, two medium, two low), all fixed; re-review approve with nits, nits addressed. Workspace tests, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean. See docs/development/ENGINE-PROTOCOL.md.

tasks.title: Run the session as the fetchpath engine: single owner, launch-or-attach, idle exit
tasks.acceptance: fetchpath engine hosts one session behind the pipe and holds the single-instance claim; any client connects or starts a detached, windowless engine and connects within a bounded wait; the engine runs while a client is connected or it has work of its own (a job queued, scheduled or running; paused jobs and failures waiting for a person are restored when a client next starts it, lead decision 24 September 2026) and exits after an idle grace period; startup recovery completes before commands are accepted; a version mismatch is refused with the contract code and the client can ask the engine to restart; an opt-in sign-in start setting exists and is off by default.
tasks.verification: Recorded 24 September 2026 on Windows 11 Pro 26200 x64: cargo test -p fetchpath --test engine 6 passed, repeated runs clean, running the real fetchpath.exe: two engines started together leave one owner; a client starts a windowless engine and a second reaches the same one; idle exit, with a scheduled job and a listening client each keeping it up; an engine killed mid-download finishes it from its checkpoint when relaunched (If-Range resume, file matches); another protocol version refused and a restart request replacing the engine; a stopping engine refuses commands while a new client reaches a fresh engine. Five mutations each failed a named test (one by hanging the suite). Workspace tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt and node --test clean. Independent strong-model review: approve with nits, all addressed. See docs/development/ENGINE-HOST.md.

tasks.title: Enforce principals, agent policy and the awaiting_approval state in the engine
tasks.acceptance: Every connection declares a principal (user, browser, agent:<name>); the engine enforces each principal policy: browser submits captures only; agents create jobs only inside granted folders, within size and rate limits, never with credentials, cookies or replace_existing, never change settings, rules, LAN, cache or sharing, and see only their own jobs. Out-of-policy requests become awaiting_approval jobs that only a user principal can approve or deny; an unknown-size job crossing the limit pauses into awaiting_approval. The job contract gains the state and its matrix rows through a superseding decision entry before code.
tasks.verification: Policy-escape tests: traversal and symlinks out of a grant, size crossing, credential smuggling, an agent approving itself or reading other jobs, settings and sharing attempts; independent strong-model review of the credential and policy boundary.

tasks.title: Make the desktop app a client of the engine
tasks.acceptance: Tauri commands become EngineClient calls and the UI updates from the event stream; closing the window no longer stops downloads and the tray reopens it; the queue, pause and resume, media, batch, schedules, checksum, details window, recovery and settings journeys behave as before; the desktop never hosts a session in-process in a shipped build.
tasks.verification: Desktop queue and recovery walkthrough and the accessibility harness pass against the engine; kill the engine during a desktop download and verify the window reports and recovers; strong-model review of the no-second-owner guarantee.

tasks.title: Hand browser captures to the engine without the desktop window
tasks.acceptance: The browser host keeps the DPAPI inbox as the durable handoff, connects as the browser principal and nudges the engine, which ingests idempotently; a capture reaches the shared queue with only the engine running; duplicates and a stopped engine still lose nothing.
tasks.verification: Browser capture tests pass with and without the desktop window; duplicate capture and engine-down cases verified.

tasks.title: Install, upgrade and uninstall with a running engine
tasks.acceptance: The installer asks a running engine to stop and waits for it to release its files before replacing them; upgrading from 0.1.0 keeps the persisted queue, history and settings; uninstall stops the engine first and keeps downloads; no engine outlives an uninstall.
tasks.verification: Upgrade over a running engine mid-download and from a 0.1.0 install with a persisted queue; uninstall with the engine running; installer tests pass; strong-model review.

tasks.title: Give the command line the whole queue through the engine
tasks.acceptance: add, ls, show, pause, resume, cancel, retry, rm, watch, inspect, batch, history, settings and engine status/stop work through the engine; job arguments accept a unique id prefix or queue index; --json prints protocol types; download keeps its arguments, streams, --quiet, --json and exit codes and now appears in the shared queue and history; lan, cache and fetch-verified are unchanged.
tasks.verification: CLI integration tests against a real engine over the pipe for every command, including exit codes 0/2/3/4/5/6/130 and --json shapes; the existing CLI tests pass unchanged.

tasks.title: Build the interactive terminal: inline live panel, prompt and slash commands
tasks.acceptance: fetchpath with no arguments in a terminal opens inline mode: finished jobs print as receipts into scrollback, a live panel shows active, paused, queued, scheduled and awaiting-approval jobs, and a prompt accepts links and / commands with completion; --plain (automatic under NO_COLOR or a dumb terminal) prints append-only lines; works in Windows Terminal and the classic console host; line-editor choice recorded after a short console probe.
tasks.verification: Render snapshot tests against recorded event streams; plain-mode output tests; keyboard-only walkthrough in Windows Terminal and conhost recorded; without a terminal it prints help and exits 2.

tasks.title: Add the full-screen dashboard with a details pane, speed graph and segments
tasks.acceptance: The inline panel already draws a bar per download and /queue lists jobs with their actions (FP-059). A key toggles a full-screen view with the queue, a details pane for the selected job (speed graph, segments and connections from the engine details data) and single-key actions with an on-screen key map; leaving restores the inline view and scrollback; resizing never corrupts the screen.
tasks.verification: Render snapshot tests at several sizes; walkthrough through the real engine including resize and toggling during a download.

tasks.title: Handle batch, conflict, checksum and approval flows in the terminal
tasks.acceptance: The link card already picks a media quality and confirms a file before it starts (FP-059). Inline prompts preview and confirm a batch of links, resolve a destination conflict without silent replacement, enter and normalize a checksum, and approve or deny an agent request with its principal, size and folder shown; every prompt can be cancelled by Esc and has a plain-mode form.
tasks.verification: Flow tests against a real engine for each prompt, including cancelling each one; an agent request approved and denied from the terminal.

tasks.title: Personalize the terminal: themes, glyphs, keybindings, aliases and custom commands
tasks.acceptance: The /settings menu already edits the engine settings (FP-059); this is the terminal's own configuration. cli.toml in the data folder holds theme, glyph set, density, keybindings and aliases; built-in themes include high-contrast and plain; /theme, /keys and /alias edit it live; aliases and custom commands expand only to Fetchpath commands and can never run a shell or external program; invalid entries are reported with their line and ignored, never fatal.
tasks.verification: Config parse and error-report tests; alias expansion tests including recursion limits and a refused shell escape; theme contrast check for built-ins.

tasks.title: Remember context: prompt history, recent folders and what happened while away
tasks.acceptance: Prompt history and completion persist across sessions with query strings and user info stripped from links by default; recent destinations and past links feed completion; opening the terminal summarizes jobs that finished or failed since it was last open, from engine history; history can be cleared with one command. CLI.md documents the history file, what is stripped and how to clear it.
tasks.verification: Tests that a signed link never reaches the history file; completion tests; summary test against engine history.

tasks.title: Apply smart rules in the engine for every client
tasks.acceptance: Rules by domain, file type or size choose destination, media quality, checksum requirement and concurrency for any principal; an agent rule-chosen folder must still be inside its grant; rules test LINK explains which rule matched and why; rules persist with the engine settings and are editable from the command line and terminal.
tasks.verification: Rule matching and precedence tests; explain output tests; an agent job whose rule points outside its grant goes to awaiting_approval.

tasks.title: Serve Fetchpath to agents as an MCP server
tasks.acceptance: fetchpath mcp speaks MCP over stdio as an agent principal with tools download, inspect_link, list_downloads, get_download, wait_for_download, pause, resume, cancel and search_history; tool schemas are generated from protocol types; progress arrives as MCP progress notifications; results mark page titles, file names and server text as untrusted; saved paths appear only inside granted folders; an observed hash is never described as publisher authenticity; setup instructions for common agent hosts are documented. The SDK is chosen from current documentation.
tasks.verification: MCP conformance tests with a scripted client; end-to-end download from a real agent host recorded; strong-model review of the agent boundary.

tasks.title: Show agent requests and agent access in the desktop and command line
tasks.acceptance: The desktop queue shows awaiting-approval jobs with approve and deny; Settings lists agents with their folders and limits and can grant, change and revoke them; fetchpath agents and fetchpath approvals do the same from the command line; revoking an agent stops its running jobs from continuing without approval.
tasks.verification: Desktop walkthrough and accessibility harness for the approval card and agent settings; CLI tests for grant, limit, revoke and approvals.

tasks.title: Attack the agent boundary and fix what breaks
tasks.acceptance: An independent reviewer derives attacks from the spec: prompt-injected titles and file names, traversal and symlinks out of grants, size-limit games, credential and cookie smuggling, self-approval, reading other principals jobs, enabling sharing or LAN, and flooding; every finding is fixed or recorded as a residual risk with a reason.
tasks.verification: Adversarial test suite added and passing; review record in docs/development with findings, fixes and residual risks.

tasks.title: Document the terminal, agents and the engine for users and contributors
tasks.acceptance: The user guide and CLI guide cover the engine, the interactive terminal, personalization, rules, approvals and agent setup, including the honest threat model; the UX contract gains terminal and agent journeys; the changelog records the platform.
tasks.verification: Every documented command and example is run against the build; node --test link checks pass.

tasks.title: Re-run the release gate on the engine platform
tasks.acceptance: The FP-018 acceptance matrix is re-run on the new architecture with added rows for the engine, terminal and agents, including a clean-machine lifecycle, upgrade over a previous build with a persisted queue, and uninstall with the engine running; the record states ready or not ready with remaining limitations. Publishing stays the user decision.
tasks.verification: Recorded matrix with commands, results and limitations in docs/development; node tools/tasks.mjs check and node --test pass.

tasks.title: Keep a queue written by a newer Fetchpath instead of discarding it
tasks.acceptance: Loading a queue whose schema is newer than this build leaves the file and its backup untouched, starts read-only with a plain explanation, and never writes over it; finding F1's characterization test is updated deliberately to the new behavior.
tasks.verification: A test writes a newer-schema queue, opens and saves repeatedly, and finds the original bytes intact; strong-model review.

tasks.title: Clear accumulated clutter so work stays on the core engine
tasks.acceptance: Scratch under work/ and the target/ build cache are cleared; merged branches and worktrees are removed. Plans, spike, review and superseded release records in docs/development are removed and listed with the commit that holds them in docs/development/ARCHIVE.md, and finished tasks cite that page. Tests are reviewed and only those guarding a contract, persisted format or invariant are kept. AGENTS.md and the workflow carry rules that stop plans, logs and evidence accumulating again. Release, installer and repository-structure checks still pass.
tasks.verification: Before/after inventory (tracked file count and bytes per area, work/ size, test count and cargo test + node --test wall time) recorded in the task evidence with the list of removed items and why; node tools/tasks.mjs check, node --test and cargo test --workspace pass.

tasks.title: Make the slow-subscriber session test fit its budget again
tasks.acceptance: a_subscriber_that_never_reads_cannot_hold_up_the_queue passes reliably on the development machine: either the 600 durable create/remove commands are made cheaper, or the test measures what it guards (the stalled subscriber cannot slow the queue) without a wall-clock budget that disk speed decides.
tasks.verification: The test passes in five consecutive workspace runs, including while another build runs; the reason for the slowdown is recorded (26 September 2026: about 92 s against 60 s in three runs, the same on e42bde5, and 42 s in a later run on a quieter machine).

tasks.title: Independent strong review of the terminal additions: link inspection, tools installer, show in folder
tasks.acceptance: A strong model that did not write them reviews commits 2b8dfff, 9779b2a and 07e7d49: InspectLink (requests made for any principal, user info refused for agents, headers only, timeouts, no body kept), the guided installer run from the terminal (pinned digests checked before install, cancellation, nothing installed without consent, --yes only for scripts), and the unsafe SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems call (COM pairing, ID list lifetime, path encoding). Findings are fixed or recorded with reasons.
tasks.verification: Findings and their resolution in the commit messages of the fixes; the touched crates’ tests and clippy pass; TERMINAL.md limitations updated if anything remains.

tasks.title: Stop showing a near-zero speed and days left as a download starts
tasks.acceptance: A download that has just started never reports a rate that does not describe its transfer, so no client shows "1 B/s" with thousands of hours left (seen in the terminal on 26 September 2026 for about a second at the start of each 24 MiB test download from a local server; the cause is not yet confirmed, and RateEstimate in the session is where the rate is computed).
tasks.verification: A unit test reproducing the start-of-download figure, then passing; the terminal walkthrough shows no such figure.

tasks.title: Apply smart rules to desktop downloads and browser captures, and manage rules in the desktop
tasks.acceptance: A browser capture is placed, and refused for a missing required checksum, by the same rule decision as a job created through the protocol; Add download proposes the matching rule folder and names the rule and why, while a folder the person picks still wins; Settings lists, adds, removes and tests rules through the engine protocol with keyboard and screen-reader support; agents still never change rules.
tasks.verification: Session tests for a capture matching a folder rule and a checksum rule; desktop end-to-end run adding a rule in Settings and seeing a pasted link and a browser capture placed by it; RULES.md limitations updated.

tasks.title: Make release terms and post-release state clear
tasks.acceptance: Before installation, the README and guide plainly say Fetchpath is free, open source and provided as is, with no warranty or promised support; they direct readers to the unchanged MIT or Apache-2.0 licenses and make user responsibility for sources and content clear. Project and release records describe the published 0.1.0 state, and signing guidance does not claim EV bypasses SmartScreen.
tasks.verification: Review the install path and license links; node tools/tasks.mjs check and node --test pass.

tasks.title: Exercise Windows power-loss recovery and publication boundaries
tasks.acceptance: An abrupt Windows VM stop during a checkpointed download and near publication is followed by restart and inspection: no unverified or partially written destination is reported complete, an existing destination remains intact, and recovery stays within the documented recoverable profile. Record the actual filesystem and VM conditions; do not promote this to a durable-mode promise from one run.
tasks.verification: Run the Windows power-interruption harness against a real build and record checksums, queue state and publication outcomes. Obtain an independent strong-model review of the persistence boundary and harness before marking done.
tasks.blockedReason: Deferred by the owner on 28 September 2026 as an optional post-release validation. A persistent Windows 11 x64 VM on NTFS with abrupt power-off control is also unavailable here. Existing process-kill and fault-injection tests do not demonstrate OS or power-loss behavior. Revisit when this validation becomes a priority: cut power during checkpoint and around publication, inspect queue and destination bytes after boot, and obtain an independent strong review. Keep the recoverable-only promise until that evidence exists.

tasks.title: Prepare browser extension store distribution without publishing
tasks.acceptance: Prepare a local extension ZIP with only the shipped Chromium files and a factual privacy disclosure suitable for a store listing. Audit permissions and native messaging identity so the remaining store-assigned ID and account steps are explicit. Do not upload, publish, or alter the installed extension until those IDs are known.
tasks.verification: Inspect ZIP contents and manifest; run extension policy tests and repository link/structure checks; record remaining store dependencies and any policy limitations.
